## Appearance

Di is a very pretty girl who features gray-green eyes that shine with a peculiar brilliance in the dusk, accompanied by red hair. She is also described as having black eyes, black hair, and rosy, dimpled cheeks that complement a merry expression.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER VIII. Anne’s Bringing-up Is Begun P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P21](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0021), [v1 CHAPTER XXX. THE INGLESIDE CHILDREN P17](../source/v05-c03.md#nw-v05-c03-p0017)_

## Personality

Di is a smart and good-natured individual who shows helpfulness toward others, such as attempting to ease a companion's toothache with cold water. Looking toward the future, she desires to travel to [Europe](../codex/places.md#europe) when she grows up.

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER VIII. Anne’s Bringing-up Is Begun P40](../source/v01-c08.md#nw-v01-c08-p0040), [v5 CHAPTER XVI. TIT FOR TAT P8](../source/v05-c16.md#nw-v05-c16-p0008), [v5 CHAPTER XXIX. A WEIRD TALE P1](../source/v05-c29.md#nw-v05-c29-p0001)_

## History

Di grew up as part of the [Blythe](../character/blythe.md) family at [Ingleside](../codex/places.md#ingleside), forming an exceptionally close bond with her brother [Walter](../character/walter.md), who shared his original poetry exclusively with her. She spent much of her childhood playing with her siblings and the neighboring Meredith children in their favorite spot, [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley), where they shared meals, stories, and dreams for the future. When [Mary Vance](../character/mary-vance.md) criticized [Faith Meredith](../character/faith.md) for a church scandal, Di and her sister [Nan](../character/nan-blythe.md) loyally defended [Faith](../character/faith.md). Di continued to spend her evenings gathered in [Rainbow Valley](../codex/places.md#rainbow-valley) with the other children, listening to [Walter](../character/walter.md) share myths and poetry, discussing local ghost stories, and hearing about everyone's aspirations. She was also present in the valley to celebrate her brother Jem's final evening with the group before he left for Queen's [Academy](../codex/places.md#queen-s-academy).

_Sources: [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P1](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0001), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P2](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0002), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P3](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0003), [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P4](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0004), [v1 CHAPTER XII. ## Quotes

> "I’m awfully glad you’ve come to live at Green Gables. It will be jolly to have somebody to play with. There isn’t any other girl who lives near enough to play with, and I’ve no sisters big enough."
>
> — Di — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P27](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0027)

> “Trees haven’t souls,” said practical Diana, “but the smell of dead fir is certainly lovely. I’m going to make a cushion and fill it with fir needles. You’d better make one too, Anne.”
>
> — Di — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P2](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0002)

> "You’re a queer girl, Anne. I heard before that you were queer. But I believe I’m going to like you real well."
>
> — Di — [v1 CHAPTER XII. A Solemn Vow and Promise P37](../source/v01-c12.md#nw-v01-c12-p0037)

> "No—not exactly. They’re like those ghost-stories of yours. They weren’t true—but you didn’t expect us to believe them, so they weren’t lies."
>
> — Di — [v5 CHAPTER VIII. MISS CORNELIA INTERVENES P16](../source/v05-c08.md#nw-v05-c08-p0016)

> "I’ve always heard that Mrs. Theodore White was the neatest woman alive and I’ll believe it after this,"
>
> — Di — [v2 VI All Sorts and Conditions of Men . . . and women P41](../source/v02-c06.md#nw-v02-c06-p0041)
